questions: Did the sensor readings give a smooth, monotonic signal across the tape, or were there dead zones or saturation at a 12 mm footprint and 40 mm spread?
Was there any integral windup or chatter needing kd, and did the 40 mm sensor spread leave the signal too coarse for the sharpest bend?
Did the robot reach a speed that finishes in under 3 s, or did base_speed or the wheel size limit the completion time?
feedback_request.suggested_changes_to_test: If the signal is too coarse, narrow the sensor spacing to 0.015 to 0.02 m total. If speed is too low, increase wheel_radius or base_speed. If the robot oscillates, reduce the sensor weights rather than adding derivative.

intent: Baseline symmetric five-sensor front array with graded weights, to establish how the geometry behaves before any tuning. Next iterations should use the Integrator's feedback and race telemetry to adjust sensor spacing, sensor size and wheel track. The aim is to keep the line in view on the tighter bends while still reaching about 1.5 m/s average speed.
learning: No prior evidence yet. Expected to learn how the 12 mm footprint and 40 mm array width trade off signal smoothness against tape-edge resolution, and whether wheel_track 0.12 m gives enough turning authority.
rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry or Integrator feedback, so this is a neutral baseline built from the contract. Five sensors spread 40 mm across the front of the body (x = -0.02 to +0.02 m, y = 0.04 m ahead of the axle) give a symmetric, graded view of the 25 mm tape. Using a 12 mm footprint, the tape covers roughly two sensors at any time, so the signal stays continuous across the line. Weights [-2,-1,0,1,2] are proportional to sensor x, so the signal is an approximate lateral offset in sensor-spacing units and is bounded by the largest weight. The wheel track of 0.12 m and wheel radius of 0.03 m are mid-range for stable turning and speed. Body width of 0.12 m keeps the off-track limit at 0.06 m, which is the floor, so a moderate excursion is tolerated. Mass of 0.8 kg is mid-range and keeps inertia moderate. Expected result: the robot completes most of the course, with the main risk being the speed needed to finish in under 3 s. base_speed 1.2 with kp 3 and kd 0.1 is a conservative start. line_loss is 'last_direction' so the robot recovers toward the side it last saw the line.
